solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leave bin out to be admired

indicators.note: words knocked out of shape are no longer in their first order, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters of the two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tidies their house by putting the bin out and hopes to be praised for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enviable is so desirable that others look on it with admiration and want it themselves.

clue.text: Current cuddly toy has lost its head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a teddy bear, the classic soft toy

explanation.surface: A child's stuffed bear has been decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as an adjective meaning present-day; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling current of water or air running against the main flow.

blocks.note: VA is the postal abbreviation of the US state
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Virginia tobacco shared out to everyone puffing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia is also a tobacco, which steers toward smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaper is someone who uses an e-cigarette, drawing in the vapour.

clue.text: Regiment in battle drama that’s broadcast repeatedly

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: soldiers see action in battle
a play is a drama
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A war film about a regiment that is shown on television again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: An action replay re-shows a moment of a sports broadcast, often several times and in slow motion.

indicators.note: remarkable can be read as re-markable, able to be marked out again in a fresh form

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: An outstanding achievement wins someone fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre in its figurative sense is glory or distinction, close to fame or renown.

blocks.note: first meaning: the cup on the green the golfer aims the ball at
second meaning: a fix or predicament, as in being in one

explanation.surface: A golfer finds the thing they are aiming for has become a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: The golfer's cup is the literal sense; the idiom of being in one gives the sense of trouble or a tight spot.

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for the police
second meaning, read literally: an aged invoice still waiting to be settled

explanation.surface: A police force whose officers have gone a long while without pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Bill is British slang for the police; the question mark flags the literal reading of a debt that has stood unsettled a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang name covers the police collectively, and taken word by word it is an overdue invoice.

blocks.note: first meaning: charming, appealing
second meaning: taking someone on as an employee

explanation.surface: A firm that is recruiting looks appealing to job-seekers.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging works as an adjective meaning charming, and as the verb form of taking on staff.

clue.text: Being out of line, am listing men for transfer

indicators.note: transferring moves things to new positions, so the letters are relocated

blocks.note: all twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer confesses to wrongly drafting men for a transfer list.
explanation.definitionFit: Misalignment is the state of not being correctly lined up, a noun synonym for being out of line.

indicators.note: one word holding another means the second sits inside the first

blocks.note: a dot is a small spot
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A shop full of records, perhaps one that spots a rare disc in the racks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record store' looks like one phrase, a music shop; the definition is only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse where goods are kept, so it is a store in the sense of a storage place.

blocks.note: the hushing sound asking for quiet
someone at home is in
slang: to dig something is to like or appreciate it

explanation.surface: Someone prefers a quiet night in to going out to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets a quiet evening against a party, yet the answer is the lively event itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal, lively celebration, a colloquial word for a party.

clue.text: Academic admitting nothing comes before studying and checking text

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word takes another inside it
placing one part ahead of another sets the order the pieces are joined

blocks.note: short for professor
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O
reading a subject at university is studying it

explanation.surface: A don concedes that nothing beats study and careful scrutiny of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreading is the job of reading through a text to spot and correct errors before it is printed.

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word's letters are taken away

blocks.note: a chart is a map, especially for sailors
taken as written before cutting
the letters removed

explanation.surface: An antique map of a cathedral has been sold on again.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartres is a famous Gothic cathedral in France, south-west of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is best known for its Gothic cathedral, so the town's name stands for the building.

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, i.e. balls bowled

explanation.surface: A man loiters around a hotel while waiting for parcels to be delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests parcels; in cricket a bowler's balls are deliveries, grouped in overs.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to linger or remain in one place, which is a synonym of hanging around.

blocks.note: surface reading: a puzzling riddle about something the admiral had
setter's reading: Nelson sailed in his flagship, and in it he won his last great battle at Trafalgar, so the ship's name and the triumph are one word

explanation.walkthrough: HMS Victory was Admiral Nelson's flagship at the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805, which he won though he died aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names both the vessel Nelson commanded from and the win he achieved while aboard it.

clue.text: Oil stirred into French wine is a fiddle

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are jumbled
putting one thing into another places it inside

blocks.note: taken as written before mixing
the French word for wine

explanation.surface: Adding oil to wine is a con, a culinary trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' reads as a swindle in the surface; here it is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle is the informal name for the violin, the bowed string instrument.

blocks.note: first meaning: small, as a ... brother is a younger one
second meaning: in folklore fairies were called the ... people

explanation.surface: In youth, folk once believed in fairies.
explanation.definitionFit: Little describes a younger sibling or child, and 'the little people' is the folk name for fairies.

clue.text: Hotel employee, first class, is German

blocks.note: in British primary schools the first year's class is called Reception
ist is the German word for is

explanation.surface: A first-class hotel's staff member turns out to be German.
explanation.walkthrough: Reception is the first class a child joins at a British primary school. 'First class' sounds like a hotel rating.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptionist works at the front desk of a hotel, greeting guests and handling bookings.

blocks.note: first meaning: prison slang for a warder, with the 's as 'is'
second meaning: old slang for a salary or pay

explanation.surface: A prison officer's pay packet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is read as 'is', not possession. Both senses are British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is old British prison slang for a guard and, separately, colloquial for someone's pay.

clue.text: A lot of elephants judged to be audible

indicators.note: something audible is heard rather than seen, so only its sound counts

blocks.note: a judge has heard a case when trying it

explanation.surface: A noisy group of elephants was assessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' sounds like an auction lot; here it simply means a large group.
explanation.definitionFit: Herd is the collective noun for a group of elephants, as for cattle.

clue.text: Brazilian diplomacy is a check on disorder

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city, shortened
tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Brazil's diplomatic skill keeps unrest under control.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was an old British law read aloud to order a crowd to disperse; to read someone the riot act is to rebuke them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was a law empowering authorities to break up unruly crowds, literally a restraint on public unrest.

clue.text: Beer with no head: that is weird

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A pint with no frothy top is a strange thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the foam on a beer; it means the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, close in sense to weird or uncanny.

indicators.note: something spoken out is said aloud, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's boy hero; his surname said in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: Mark Twain's Tom is a cheeky, mouthy boy — full of sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' reads as cheek, fitting the outspoken boy; it is the condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya is short for soy sauce, the salty condiment brewed from fermented soybeans.

blocks.note: the finest is the best
a debt outstanding is still owed

explanation.surface: Admittedly, the very best is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as excellent; it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to confer or give, so bestowed is a past-tense synonym of granted.
